title: "units::set_units() takes the variable name for the unit"
ref: TDY-16
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: silencieux

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
library(units)
x <- 1:3
u <- "km"
set_units(x, u)
set_units(set_units(x, u), value = "g", mode = "standard")

target <- "km"
set_units(x, target)
```

```text
Units: [u]
[1] 1 2 3
Units: [g]
[1] 1.660540e-24 3.321080e-24 4.981621e-24
Error: In 'target', 'target' is not recognized by udunits.
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the {units} package, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

`set_units()` reads its second argument without evaluating it, so that you can write `set_units(x, m)` or `set_units(x, km/h)` without quotes. The symbol `u` is therefore never replaced by its value `"km"`: it is taken as is, as a unit name. And `u` exists: it is the atomic mass unit. The values become masses, and convert to grams without a murmur.

With a variable name that is not a unit, such as `target`, you at least get an error. The trap only snaps shut on short names that are also units: `u`, `m`, `g`, `s`, `h`...

## The remedy

Pass the unit as text, with `mode = "standard"`, which evaluates the argument normally.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
set_units(x, value = u, mode = "standard")
set_units(x, value = "km", mode = "standard")
```

```text
Units: [km]
[1] 1 2 3
Units: [km]
[1] 1 2 3
```
:::
